title: Fixed Compact Keybed and Open Mouthpiece Melodica
description: One newly authored complete fixed melodica-inspired exterior. One low elongated chamfered shell contains a genuine shallow recessed keybed and an intact finite lower body. Eighteen whole pale keys seat in that bed with visible longitudinal gaps, and thirteen whole short dark keys sit proud in a deliberately simplified grouped pattern. One continuous short mouthpiece roots in the left side: its external tube broadens into a flattened lip with a real open central passage and full inner wall. Two entire narrow lower resting feet ground the complete instrument. The compact single wind-keyboard-body organization is newly authored together; unlike the two deep accordion end cases there is no connecting bellows or separate button bank, unlike the pocket harmonica there is no exposed ten-channel comb between two curved covers, and unlike the full pipe organ there are no tall pipes, floor console, stop controls or pedal bed. No old instrument part is imported, removed or resized; all profiles and key coordinates are new. Thirty-five closed editable whole meshes, four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal-bounds-centred ground origin. One original model zero scenes; keys are subordinate parts, not counted assets. Unbranded generic static appearance, not an exact product, pitch range, authentic key mechanism or measured instrument. The visible mouthpiece bore is modeled only to its seated root; hidden reeds, valves, internal air communication and chamber construction are not supplied or verified. No air tube accessory, text, notes, logos, player, sound, breath flow, tuning, playing, key travel, mouth contact suitability, hygiene, ergonomics, load, materials, manufacture or safety capability. No rigging animation or interaction.
